Class BidiMappingService

java.lang.Object
org.openehealth.ipf.commons.map.BidiMappingService
All Implemented Interfaces:
MappingService
Direct Known Subclasses:
SpringBidiMappingService
@Deprecated(since="6.0", forRemoval=true) public class BidiMappingService extends Object implements MappingService
Deprecated, for removal: This API element is subject to removal in a future version.
as of 6.0, use Mappings - DefaultMappings is the implementation to build on, and SpringMappings in ipf-commons-spring the bean to wire. This class remains as an adapter for applications still holding a MappingService, and is scheduled for removal in IPF 7.0.
MappingService implementation backed by Mappings, which is where the actual model and the loading of mapping sources live as of IPF 6.0.

This class exists to keep the untyped, null-returning MappingService contract working for existing applications. It answers exactly what Mappings answers, with null where that returns an empty Optional.

Two conventions of the Groovy implementation it replaces are gone:

  • an empty value is a value: an entry mapping to "" yields "", rather than the mapping's fallback, and a default passed in applies only where there is no value at all;
  • there is no composite convention: a value containing ~ is returned as the string it is rather than as a List, and a Collection passed as a key or value is rejected rather than joined. A mapping whose keys or values consist of several parts must either be split into separate mappings, or the calling code joins and splits the parts itself.

New code should use Mappings directly — it is String-typed and returns Optional. getMappings() hands out the instance this service delegates to.

Mapping sources are dispatched to a MappingLoader by file extension, so the format of a mapping file is a decision per file. Reading the legacy .map script format needs ipf-commons-map-groovy on the classpath.

As of version 3.1, the add/setMappingScript(Resource) methods have been out-factored into the class SpringBidiMappingService located in the ipf-commons-spring module.

    • setMappingFunctions

      public void setMappingFunctions(Map<String, Function<String,String>> functions)
      Deprecated, for removal: This API element is subject to removal in a future version.
      Registers the functions that a mapping's computed fallback refers to by name, i.e. what <unmatched mode="function" ref="..."/> resolves against. A function receives the key that had no entry and returns the value for it, so a mapping can derive its answer from its input rather than list it: 
      mappingService.setMappingFunctions(Map.of(
        "first4", key -> key == null || key.length() <= 4 ? key : key.substring(0, 4)));
      A mapping source naming a function that is not registered is rejected as it is read, so register them first. As a Spring bean property that happens before any configurer adds mapping resources; a module that ships both a mapping file and the function it names should contribute a MappingFunctionProvider instead.
      Parameters:
      functions - functions by name, replacing any registered under the same name before
